mainTopic: Binding marriage promises made by words alone, whether they may be written, and where a daughter lives
overview: This amud opens by finishing an argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. Both follow רבי ישמעאל, but ריש לקיש limits his rule to cases where a Torah-level debt already exists. The גמרא then quotes רב: when two families state what each will give their child, and the couple do קידושין, those promises bind through words alone. רבא first limits this to the father of a נערה, then swears that it applies even to a בוגרת. His reason is that the joy of the families joining is what makes them commit. רבינא and רב אשי discuss whether such spoken promises may be written down. רב אשי says no and defends this against three proofs from משניות. The last proof leads to a long discussion of why the wife's daughter can collect from sold property but the husbands' own daughters cannot. Finally, רב חסדא learns from the משנה that a daughter lives with her mother. The גמרא challenges this with a ברייתא about a child kept from his heirs for safety, and the defense of רב חסדא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Both sides follow רבי ישמעאל, and רבי יוחנן applies him plainly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the argument is not רבי ישמעאל against the רבנן. Both אמוראים agree with רבי ישמעאל, and רבי יוחנן applies his view straightforwardly.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they argue, it is within רבי ישמעאל's view. רבי יוחנן simply follows רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier discussion. It explains that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both hold like רבי ישמעאל, and that רבי יוחנן applies his ruling to our case too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא suggested that the argument matched the older argument of רבי ישמעאל and the רבנן about a ערב (guarantor). Now it changes the picture: both follow רבי ישמעאל. For רבי יוחנן, רבי ישמעאל's rule that words alone can obligate a person carries over to our case as well.

keyTerms.meaning: When they argue (where the argument really lies)
According to the view of

phrases.english: When they argue, it is according to רבי ישמעאל.
phrases.notes: "They" means רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, from the argument just before this.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן holds like רבי ישמעאל (plainly),

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier suggestion that the argument follows the older argument between רבי ישמעאל and the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the argument: both follow one תנא and disagree only about how far his rule reaches.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש split along the lines of רבי ישמעאל against the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both accept רבי ישמעאל. רבי יוחנן applies his rule fully to our case.

steps.title: ריש לקיש limits רבי ישמעאל to a Torah-level debt
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says רבי ישמעאל only made a person liable through words where a Torah-level debt already exists. In our case there is none.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש says: רבי ישמעאל only said his rule there, because it connects to a Torah-level debt. Here, no Torah-level debt is involved.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains why he can follow רבי ישמעאל and still disagree with רבי יוחנן. He says רבי ישמעאל's case is different from ours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי ישמעאל's case there is a real loan, and a loan creates a debt from the Torah, so a guarantor's words can attach to it. In our case nobody owed anything before the promise. A bare promise has no Torah-level debt to attach to, so even רבי ישמעאל would say the person does not have to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said his ruling up to this point (in this case)
A Torah-level debt or obligation
Relates to, applies to

steps.whatToRemember: Both אמוראים follow רבי ישמעאל. ריש לקיש limits his rule to cases where a Torah-level debt already exists, and a simple promise is not such a case.

phrases.english: And ריש לקיש says:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הָתָם
phrases.english: רבי ישמעאל only said his rule there
phrases.notes: "There" is the guarantor case discussed just before.

phrases.english: because it is connected to a Torah-level debt,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא לָא שָׁיֵיךְ שִׁיעְבּוּדָא דְאוֹרָיְיתָא.
phrases.english: but here no Torah-level debt is involved.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives ריש לקיש's side of the argument that step 1 placed within רבי ישמעאל's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases: a Torah-level debt versus a bare promise.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רבי ישמעאל should force ריש לקיש to obligate the person as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל's rule needs an existing Torah-level debt, which is missing here.

steps.title: רב: wedding-gift promises become binding through words
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל quotes רב: if two families state how much each will give their child, and the couple then do קידושין, the promises are binding with no קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main topic. רב גידל said in the name of רב: one side asks, "How much are you giving your son?" The answer is, "This much." "And how much are you giving your daughter?" "This much." If the couple then went ahead and did קידושין, the promises are acquired. These are the things that are acquired through speech alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a statement it mentioned earlier and now quotes it in full. רב rules that promises made in marriage talks become binding once the couple do קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a promise of money needs a formal act of acquisition (קנין) to be binding. רב says that here spoken words are enough, as long as the קידושין actually happened. This is the special category of "things acquired by speech" (דברים הנקנים באמירה).

keyTerms.meaning: Back to the statement itself (returning to a source quoted earlier)
Such and such (a stated amount)
They went ahead and did קידושין
Acquired through speech alone

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that promises made during שידוכין are binding without a קנין once קידושין take place.

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Back to the statement itself: רב גידל said in the name of רב:
"How much are you giving your son?"
"Such and such."
"And how much are you giving your daughter?"
"Such and such."
If they went ahead and did קידושין, the promises are acquired,
these are the very things that are acquired through speech.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש discussion and returns to רב's statement quoted earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Amounts promised during marriage talks become binding through words alone once the couple perform קידושין.

steps.title: רבא limits רב's rule to a daughter who is a נערה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רב's rule makes sense when the daughter is a נערה, because then her father gains from the קידושין. It would not apply to a בוגרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רב's statement makes sense for a man whose daughter is a נערה, since he gets a benefit. But for a בוגרת, where he gets no benefit, it does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא suggests narrowing רב's rule. He says it only applies when the bride's father is getting something out of the קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reasoning is that a person commits himself by words alone when he receives a benefit in return. A father receives the קידושין money of a daughter who is a נערה, so he gains. A בוגרת receives her own קידושין money, so her father gains nothing, and by this reasoning his promise would not bind him.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, it is reasonable
A young girl (from about 12 to 12½) whose קידושין money goes to her father
A grown woman (past 12½) who receives her own קידושין money
Benefit, gain

steps.confusionAlert: This is not רבא's final view. In the very next line he takes it back.

phrases.english: רבא said: רב's statement makes sense
for a man whose daughter is a נערה,
since a benefit reaches his hands,
but a בוגרת,
where no benefit reaches his hands, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the scope of רב's ruling from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposed limit: the father is bound only when he gains from the קידושין, which happens when the daughter is a נערה.

steps.title: רבא swears that רב meant even a בוגרת
steps.stepSummary: רבא takes back his limit and declares strongly that רב's rule applies even to a בוגרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: By God! רב said it even about a בוגרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects his own suggestion from the step before. He uses an oath to show how sure he now is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limit based on the father's benefit is dropped. רב's rule now covers a father of a בוגרת as well, even though he receives no money from the קידושין. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: By God! (a strong oath showing certainty)
Even

phrases.english: By God!
רב said it even about a בוגרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא withdraws the limit he set in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the limit of רב's rule to a daughter who is a נערה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Benefit to the father cannot be the reason, as the next step proves.

steps.title: Proof: the groom's father gets no money either
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that the groom's father receives no money benefit, yet רב's rule binds him too. So money benefit cannot be the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if you don't say so, what benefit does the groom's father get?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves his new position. The groom's father is also bound by his promise in רב's case, yet he gains nothing in money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's case includes both fathers promising. The groom's father never receives any קידושין money. If benefit were needed, his promise would not count, but רב treats it as binding. So the reason must be something other than money benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: Because if you do not say so
The groom's father

phrases.english: Because if you don't say so,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבִי הַבֵּן מַאי הֲנָאָה אֲתָא לִידֵיהּ?
phrases.english: what benefit comes into the groom's father's hands?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, אֲבִי הַבֵּן מַאי הֲנָאָה אֲתָא לִידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבא's retraction in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That רב's rule applies even to the father of a בוגרת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's own case binds the groom's father, who gains no money.

steps.title: The real reason: the joy of the families marrying each other
steps.stepSummary: The fathers commit fully to each other because of the satisfaction of becoming related through marriage, not because of any money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, because of that benefit, that they are marrying into each other's families, they fully commit and transfer to each other.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the true reason behind רב's rule, which wraps up this discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "benefit" is not money. It is the joy and closeness of the two families joining through marriage. That feeling is strong enough that each father wholeheartedly binds himself to his promise, so the rule applies to both fathers and to a בוגרת as well.

keyTerms.meaning: They are marrying into each other's families
They fully commit and transfer ownership
To each other

steps.whatToRemember: רב's rule applies to both fathers and even to a בוגרת. The binding force comes from the satisfaction of the families joining through marriage, not from any money benefit.

phrases.english: Rather, through that benefit,
that they are marrying into each other's families,
they fully commit and transfer ownership to each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised by the proof in step 6 by naming the real benefit.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The commitment comes from the satisfaction of the two families joining through marriage, so רב's rule covers both fathers and even a בוגרת.

steps.title: May these spoken promises be written down?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי whether the spoken marriage promises may be written as a formal document.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Are these matters allowed to be written, or not allowed to be written?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא asks a new question about the binding spoken promises from רב's rule: may they be put into a written document?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know the promises are binding without a קנין. The new question is about their form. Can they be recorded as a proper legal document, or must they stay as spoken commitments only?

keyTerms.meaning: Allowed to be written (as a formal document)

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
Are these matters allowed to be written,
phrases.notes: 'These matters' are the spoken promises between the two families from רב's rule.

phrases.english: or not allowed to be written?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבָרִים הַלָּלוּ נִיתְּנוּ לִיכָּתֵב, אוֹ לֹא נִיתְּנוּ לִיכָּתֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב's rule about binding spoken promises and asks a new practical question about them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the spoken promises may be written as a formal document.

steps.title: They may not be written
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that these promises are not allowed to be written.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: They are not allowed to be written.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives his answer: the promises may not be written as a formal document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the promises are binding, but only as spoken words. They cannot be turned into a formal written document. The next steps will test this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Were not given permission, not allowed

phrases.english: He said to him:
They are not allowed to be written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The spoken promises may not be written as a formal document.

steps.title: Challenge: the smart ones would write
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges from a משנה that says the smart ones would write a condition into the agreement.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised an objection: The smart ones would write, 'On condition that I will feed your daughter for five years, as long as you are with me'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks רב אשי's answer with a משנה that seems to show people did write these marriage agreements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the word 'write' about a promise made at marriage. That suggests such promises can be written, which goes against רב אשי.

keyTerms.meaning: Smart, careful people
On condition that
I will feed or support

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
The smart ones would write:
phrases.notes: This is from our פרק's משנה (101b), about a man who promised to support his new wife's daughter.

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל מְנָת שֶׁאָזוּן אֶת בִּתֵּךְ חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים
phrases.english: "On condition that I will feed your daughter for five years
as long as you are with me"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אשי's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's ruling that the promises may not be written.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says the smart ones 'would write' such a condition, so these agreements can be written.

steps.title: 'Write' here means 'say'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that 'write' in that משנה means 'say'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'write' mean? They say.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends himself by reading the word 'write' in the משנה as 'say'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the smart ones only said the condition out loud, the משנה is no proof that it may be written. The challenge goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: What, what does it mean
They say

phrases.english: What does "write" mean here?
They say.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by reinterpreting a word.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Write' means actually putting it in a document.

steps.title: Can saying be called writing?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא questions whether the משנה would really call speaking 'writing'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does he call saying 'writing'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes back on רב אשי's answer: is it really normal to call speaking 'writing'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is on the answer itself. Reading 'write' as 'say' looks forced, so רב אשי needs to show the משנה really speaks this way.

keyTerms.meaning: Saying, speech
Writing

phrases.english: And does he call saying "writing"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'write' does not naturally mean 'say', so the reading seems forced.

steps.title: Yes, as רבי חייא taught
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי proves from another משנה, explained by רבי חייא, that 'write' can mean 'say'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. And we learned: 'One who writes to his wife, I have no claim or involvement in your property.' And רבי חייא taught: 'One who says to his wife.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers 'yes' and brings a case where the משנה says 'writes' and רבי חייא explains it means 'says'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that 'writing' is a known way for the משנה to describe speaking. So reading the smart ones' 'writing' as speaking is not forced, and רב אשי's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Claim and involvement, legal dealings
Property

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי holds the promises may not be written, and he reads 'write' in the משנה as 'say', just as רבי חייא did in another case.

phrases.english: Yes, and we learned in a mishna:
One who writes to his wife:
"I have no claim or involvement in your property,"
and Rabbi Ḥiyya taught:
One who says to his wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12 with a proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a parallel use of language
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה does use 'write' to mean 'say', as רבי חייא shows.
steps.raayaObject: That 'write' can mean 'say' in the משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה 'one who writes to his wife', explained by רבי חייא as 'one who says'.

steps.title: Challenge from documents of betrothal and marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה that allows writing betrothal and marriage documents with both sides' consent, and suggests these are the promise documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: We do not write documents of betrothal and marriage except with the consent of both of them. This implies that with the consent of both, we do write. Is it not referring to documents of the agreed amounts?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to רב אשי from a משנה about writing marriage documents. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה implies that with both sides' agreement, such documents may be written. If those documents record what each family promised, they are exactly what רב אשי said may not be written.

keyTerms.meaning: Documents of betrothal and marriage
With the consent of both of them
Is it not that, introducing a suggested reading
Documents recording the amounts each side promised

phrases.english: Come and hear:
We do not write documents of betrothal and marriage
phrases.notes: This משנה is in בבא בתרא (167b).

phrases.english: except with the consent of both of them.
This implies: with the consent of both of them, we do write.
Is it not referring to documents of stipulation!
phrases.notes: These are documents listing what each family promised, the same promises from רב's rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אֵין כּוֹתְבִין שְׁטָרֵי אֵירוּסִין וְנִשּׂוּאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, opens a second challenge against רב אשי's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's ruling that the spoken promises may not be written.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies that with both sides' consent these documents may be written, and they seem to be documents of the promised amounts.

steps.title: The משנה means real betrothal documents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 14. The משנה is about actual betrothal documents, not promise documents, and it follows רב פפא and רב שרביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means actual betrothal documents, following the view of רב פפא and רב שרביא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from step 14. It says the משנה is not talking about promise agreements at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14, the גמרא suggested that 'betrothal documents' meant the written promise agreements. Now it says the words mean real betrothal documents, the kind a man gives a woman to make her his wife. Such a document needs both sides' consent, so the משנה teaches nothing about whether a spoken promise can be written down.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal documents: a document a man gives a woman to betroth her
Actual, literally
Following the view of רב פפא

phrases.english: No, it means actual betrothal documents.
In accordance with Rav Pappa and Rav Sherevya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the משנה offered in step 14
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The identification of 'betrothal documents' in the משנה as promise documents
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be read literally, as real betrothal documents that need both sides' consent

steps.title: Dispute over a betrothal document written without her consent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the dispute behind step 15. If a betrothal document was written for a specific woman but without her consent, רבה and רבינא say she is betrothed, and רב פפא and רב שרביא say she is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: if he wrote it for her but without her knowledge, רבה and רבינא say she is betrothed; רב פפא and רב שרביא say she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the dispute it just pointed to. This shows why a betrothal document needs both sides' consent according to one view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires the consent of both sides when writing betrothal documents. That fits רב פפא and רב שרביא, who say a document written without her consent does not betroth her. So the משנה is about real betrothal, which supports the rejection in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: For her sake, written for this specific woman
With her knowledge and consent
She is betrothed

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree the document was written for this specific woman. They argue only about whether her consent is also needed.

phrases.english: As it was stated: if he wrote it for her sake,
but without her knowledge,
Rabba and Ravina say: she is betrothed;

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב שֵׁרֵבְיָא אָמְרִי: אֵינָהּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת.
phrases.english: Rav Pappa and Rav Sherevya say: she is not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the dispute that step 15 relied on
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב פפא and רב שרביא, a betrothal document written without the woman's consent does not betroth her, so both sides must agree to its writing

steps.title: The wife's daughter collects like a creditor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another משנה. After the husbands die, their own daughters are supported from free property, but the wife's daughter is supported even from sold property, because she is like a creditor. That suggests her promise was written in a document.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if they died, their daughters are supported from free property, and she is supported even from sold property, because she is like a creditor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof that a spoken promise can be written down. It uses the משנה about husbands who promised to support the wife's daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually only a creditor with a document can take back property the debtor already sold. The wife's daughter can do that, so the husbands' promise must have been written down. If so, a promise made by speech alone can be put into a document.

keyTerms.meaning: Free property: property the dead man still owned and had not sold
Liened property: property that was sold but is still tied to an earlier debt
A creditor (a woman who is owed money)

phrases.english: Come and hear: if they died,
phrases.notes: 'They' are the two husbands who each promised to support the wife's daughter.

phrases.english: their daughters are supported from free property,
and she is supported even from liened property,
phrases.notes: 'She' is the wife's daughter from an earlier marriage.

phrases.english: because she is like a creditor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in step 14 was rejected, a new proof is brought
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that promises made by speech alone cannot be written into a document
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Collecting from sold property needs a document. The daughter collects from sold property, so her promise must have been written down.

steps.title: There was a formal act of acquisition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about husbands who made a formal קנין, not just a spoken promise, so a document may be written.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where they made a קנין from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by narrowing the case in that משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husbands did a formal act of acquisition, the obligation is fully binding and can be written down like any debt. So this משנה proves nothing about a promise made by words alone.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Introduces a narrower reading of a source
They made a קנין from him: a formal act of acquisition that confirms an obligation

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
Where they made a formal acquisition from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the wife's daughter collecting from sold property
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case involves a formal קנין, so the document comes from the קנין and not from speech alone

steps.title: Then their own daughters should also collect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if a קנין was made, why can't the husbands' own daughters also collect from sold property?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the daughters should also collect from sold property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husbands made a formal קנין, it seems their own daughters' support should also be fully binding. Then the daughters should collect from sold property too. But the משנה says they collect only from free property.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a challenge to the answer just given
Also

phrases.english: If so, the daughters too!
phrases.notes: He means the husbands' own daughters should also collect from sold property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a קנין was made
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קנין should strengthen the daughters' claim as well, yet the משנה treats them differently

steps.title: The קנין was made only for the wife's daughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the קנין was made for the wife's daughter but not for the husbands' own daughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they made a קנין for this one and not for that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining that only one daughter's support was confirmed with a קנין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the wife's daughter got a formal קנין, so only she collects like a creditor, even from sold property. The husbands' own daughters had no קנין, so they collect only from free property. The proof from step 17 stays rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: For this one and not for that one

steps.whatToRemember: All three proofs against רב אשי so far have been turned aside. The wife's daughter collects from sold property because a formal קנין was made for her. Why the husbands' own daughters are treated differently is worked out in the next steps.

phrases.english: Where they made a formal acquisition for this one and did not make one for that one.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the wife's daughter. 'That one' is the husbands' own daughters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the קנין applied to only one party
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A קנין by the husbands would cover all the daughters' support
steps.terutzMaskana: The קנין covered only the wife's daughter, so only she collects like a creditor

steps.title: Why is the case so clear-cut?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we should assume the קנין covered the wife's daughter but not the husbands' own daughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what makes it so clear-cut?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the answer in step 20. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will explain the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said the קנין was made for the wife's daughter and not for the husbands' daughters. That sounds like it could just as easily have gone the other way. So the גמרא wants a reason why the case is always split this way.

keyTerms.meaning: What makes it clear-cut? (Why is the case always this way?)

phrases.english: And what makes it clear-cut?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the distinction made in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why we assume the קנין covered only the wife's daughter and not the husbands' daughters.

steps.title: Only the wife's daughter was alive at the time of the קנין
steps.stepSummary: The wife's daughter was already alive when the קנין was made, so it works for her. The husbands' daughters were not yet born, so it does not work for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: She was there at the time of the קנין, so the קנין works for her. The daughters were not there at the time of the קנין, so the קנין does not work for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference comes from timing. The wife's daughter already existed when the קנין was made, but the husbands' daughters were born later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קנין can only take effect for someone who exists when it is made. The wife's daughter came from an earlier marriage, so she was already born. The husbands' own daughters were born only after the wedding, so the קנין could not cover them.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time the formal acquisition was made
It works / it takes effect

phrases.english: She, who was there at the time of the קנין:
phrases.notes: 'She' means the wife's daughter from an earlier marriage.

phrases.english: the קנין works for her.
The daughters, who were not there at the time of the קנין:
the קנין does not work for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is timing. The wife's daughter existed when the קנין was made, and the husbands' daughters did not.

steps.title: The husbands' daughters could also have been alive at the time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that a husband's daughter could also have been alive at the time of the קנין, if he divorced his wife and later remarried her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can't we be talking about a case where they were there at the time of the קנין? How could that happen? For example, if he divorced her and then took her back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the timing answer. It shows a case where a husband's own daughter was already born when the קנין was made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose a husband divorced his wife after they had a daughter, and then he married her again. At the second marriage, his daughter is already alive. The timing answer does not explain why she still cannot collect from sold property.

keyTerms.meaning: Aren't we also dealing with (a case where...)?
And how would that case look?
He divorced her and took her back

phrases.aramaic: מִי לָא עָסְקִינַן דַּהֲוַאי בִּשְׁעַת קִנְיָן,
phrases.english: Are we not dealing with a case where they were there at the time of the קנין?
And how would that look?
For example, where he divorced her and took her back!
phrases.notes: A daughter born in the first marriage is already alive when the second marriage's קנין is made.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא עָסְקִינַן דַּהֲוַאי בִּשְׁעַת קִנְיָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the timing answer of step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the husbands' daughters were never present at the time of the קנין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A remarriage case shows a husband's daughter can exist at the time of the קנין. Yet the משנה still does not let her collect from sold property.

steps.title: The husbands' daughters are already covered by the court's rule
steps.stepSummary: The new answer is that the wife's daughter is not covered by the תנאי בית דין, so the קנין helps her. The husbands' daughters are already covered by it, so the קנין does not help them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: she is not part of the court's stipulation, so the קנין works for her. The daughters are part of the court's stipulation, so the קנין does not work for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the timing answer and gives a new one. The difference is that the husbands' own daughters already have support rights from the תנאי בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the תנאי בית דין, a man must support his own daughters. His wife's daughter from another man is not covered by that rule. So the קנין is what gives her rights, while the husbands' daughters stay under the court's rule instead.

keyTerms.meaning: A condition the court builds into every marriage, such as a father supporting his daughters
She is not included / they are included

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: אִיהִי דְּלֵיתַאּ בִּתְנַאי בֵּית דִּין —
phrases.english: Rather: she, who is not included in the court's stipulation:
the קנין works for her.
The daughters, who are included in the court's stipulation:
the קנין does not work for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אִיהִי דְּלֵיתַאּ בִּתְנַאי בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected timing answer with a new distinction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference was whether the daughter existed at the time of the קנין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is whether the daughter is already covered by the תנאי בית דין.

steps.title: Should being covered by the court make them worse off?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why being covered by the תנאי בית דין should weaken the husbands' daughters. It should help them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they made weaker?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 24 with a short, sharp question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנאי בית דין gives the husbands' daughters a right to support. An extra right should make their claim stronger, not weaker. So step 24 seems backwards.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they made weaker / worse off?

phrases.english: Are they made worse off?
phrases.notes: He means that being covered by the court's rule should only add to their rights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the logic of step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that being included in the תנאי בית דין stops the קנין from helping the husbands' daughters.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Having an extra right should not cancel the benefit of the קנין. It should only add to their rights.

steps.title: We suspect the father already gave his daughters money
steps.stepSummary: Since a father must support his daughters under the תנאי בית דין, we suspect he already gave them bundles of money before he died. So they cannot take back sold property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is the reason for his daughters: since they are included in the court's stipulation, we can say he already gave them bundles of money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final reason. The husbands' daughters cannot collect from sold property because their father may already have given them money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court's rule does not weaken the daughters' rights. Instead, because fathers know they must support their daughters, they often set money aside for them. That creates a doubt about whether the daughters are still owed anything. There is no such doubt about the wife's daughter, since he had no court duty to her.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the reason
Bundles (of money)
He handed them over / gave them to hold

steps.whatToRemember: The wife's daughter can collect from sold property because the קנין gave her a real claim. The husbands' own daughters cannot, because we suspect their father already gave them money during his lifetime.
steps.confusionAlert: The תנאי בית דין does not make the husbands' daughters weaker. It only raises the suspicion that they were already paid.

phrases.english: Rather, for his daughters, this is the reason:
since they are included in the court's stipulation,
we can say he gave them bundles of money.
phrases.notes: We worry that the father already provided for them before he died, so they may not take land back from buyers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25 with a new reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being under the תנאי בית דין stops the קנין from working for the husbands' daughters.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קנין may cover them too, but we suspect the father already gave them money, so they cannot take back sold property.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finally answers the question of step 19. It explains why only the wife's daughter is treated like a creditor who can collect from sold property.

steps.title: A daughter lives with her mother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that the first husband cannot make the girl come to him for food. רב חסדא learns from it that a daughter stays with her mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says the first husband may not say 'let her come to me to eat.' רב חסדא said: this shows that a daughter lives with her mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. רב חסדא draws a general rule from it: a daughter belongs with her mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the husband must bring the food to where the mother lives. רב חסדא reasons that the משנה would only say this if the girl's normal place is with her mother. So he turns one detail in the משנה into a general rule for divorce cases.

keyTerms.meaning: The first husband, who agreed to support his wife's daughter
'This is to say': a rule learned from a source
A daughter stays with her mother

phrases.english: The first [husband] may not say.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: he can't insist the girl come to him to eat. He has to send the food to where her mother lives.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
This is to say: a daughter is with her mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, separate from the earlier discussion about the תנאי בית דין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A daughter lives with her mother, as shown by the משנה's ruling that the food goes to the mother's place.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה only means a young girl, for her safety
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the משנה means an older girl. Maybe it means a young girl, kept with her mother only for safety because of a past incident.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know we are dealing with an older girl? Maybe we are dealing with a young girl, and the reason is a story that once happened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's rule. Maybe the משנה is only about a young girl, kept with her mother for a special safety reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's rule works only if the משנה is about any daughter, including a גדולה. If the משנה is about a קטנה, she may stay with her mother only because of danger, and no general rule follows. The גמרא hints at a 'story that happened' and brings it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do we know?
An adult girl
A minor girl
An incident that once happened

phrases.english: From where [do we know] that we are dealing with an adult girl?
Perhaps we are dealing with a minor girl,
and because of an incident that happened.

steps.triggerLanguage: ממאי דבגדולה עסקינן דלמא בקטנה עסקינן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's inference by offering another way to read the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's general rule that a daughter lives with her mother.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה is about a קטנה, she stays with her mother only for safety. So the משנה does not prove a general rule about where a daughter lives.

steps.title: The ברייתא about the boy killed by his heirs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the ברייתא behind the 'incident.' A young orphan is left with his mother, not with the people who would inherit him, because once such heirs killed a child.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: if a man died and left a young son, the father's heirs say 'let him grow up with us,' and the mother says 'let my son grow up with me.' We leave him with his mother, not with someone who would inherit him. It once happened that they slaughtered him on ערב פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a ברייתא. It shows that a young child is kept with his mother for safety reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא rules against leaving a child with people who would gain from his death, because once such heirs murdered a child. This supports the challenge: the משנה may keep a קטנה with her mother only to protect her, not because of a general rule about daughters.

keyTerms.meaning: The father's heirs
Someone who stands to inherit the child
The day before פסח

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is not a proof for רב חסדא. It supports the challenge against him, giving a safety reason for keeping a child with the mother.

phrases.english: As it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁמֵּת וְהִנִּיחַ בֵּן קָטָן לְאִמּוֹ,
phrases.english: One who died and left a minor son with his mother,
the father's heirs say:
Let him grow up with us,
and his mother says:
Let my son grow up with me —
we leave him with his mother,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מַנִּיחִין אוֹתוֹ אֵצֶל רָאוּי לְיוֹרְשׁוֹ.
phrases.english: and we do not leave him with one who is fit to inherit him.
An incident happened
and they slaughtered him on the eve of Pesach!

steps.triggerLanguage: דתניא מי שמת והניח בן קטן לאמו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the 'incident that happened' mentioned in the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That a young child may be kept with the mother only for safety, which weakens רב חסדא's general rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא ruling that an orphan stays with his mother and not his heirs, because of a case where heirs killed a child.

steps.title: The משנה's wording points to the mother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins defending רב חסדא. If safety were the reason, the משנה should have said 'the place where she is,' not 'her mother's place.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the משנה say: '[he brings the food] to the place where she is.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the challenge by looking closely at the משנה's words. The answer continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only concern were keeping the girl away from danger, the משנה could simply say the food goes to wherever she is. Instead it says the food goes to her mother's place. That wording suggests the girl's normal home is with her mother, which supports רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let it teach: the משנה should have said
To the place where she is

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: If the reason is only safety for a young girl.

phrases.english: let it teach: 'to the place where she is,'
phrases.notes: The משנה actually says the food goes to her mother's place. The גמרא finishes this point in the next lines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 28-29 by pointing to the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the משנה's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה keeps only a young girl with her mother, and only for her safety.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה names the mother's place, not just wherever the girl is. This supports רב חסדא's rule that a daughter lives with her mother. The answer is completed in the next lines.
